'''Ruth Arnon''' ({{Langx|he|רות ארנון}} [ʁut aʁ'non]; born in [[Tel Aviv]] on June 1, 1933) is an Israeli [[biochemist]] and codeveloper of the [[multiple sclerosis]] drug [[Copaxone]]. She is currently the Paul Ehrlich Professor of Immunology at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]], where she is researching anti-cancer and [[Influenza vaccine|influenza vaccinations]].

==Biography==

Ruth Rosenberg (later Arnon) was born in [[Tel Aviv]], the youngest of three children.<ref>[https://www.haaretz.com/science-and-health/2020-05-06/ty-article-magazine/.premium/could-the-flu-become-history-an-israeli-vaccine-may-make-it-a-reality/0000017f-db5b-db22-a17f-fffb220f0000 Could the flu become history? An Israeli vaccine may do just that], [[Haaretz]]</ref> Her father, Alexander Rosenberg, moved with the family to Toulouse to pursue degrees in electrical engineering and mathematics.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Shalvi |first=Alice |title=Ruth Arnon |url=https://jwa.org/encyclopedia/article/arnon-ruth |access-date=2026-09-24 |website=Jewish Women's Archive |publisher=Jewish Women's Archive |language=en}}</ref> Upon their return to Israel, he worked for the [[Israel Electric Corporation]].<ref name=":1" /> Arnon says her desire to study was inspired by her father.<ref name=":1" /> She attended [[Herzliya Hebrew Gymnasium]] and knew she wanted to be a medical researcher by the age of 15.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Ruth and Uriel Arnon |url=https://www.weizmann.ac.il/WeizmannCompass/sections/people-behind-the-science/ruth-and-uriel-arnon |access-date=2026-09-24 |website=www.weizmann.ac.il |language=en}}</ref> She studied chemistry at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], earning her M.Sc. degree in 1955 and served in the IDF.<ref name=":3" /> During her time in the military, she married Uriel Arnon, an engineer at the Technion in Haifa.  They have two children: Michal (b. 1957) and Yoram (b. 1961).<ref name=":1" />

==Scientific career==
In 1957, Arnon began to work on her doctorate under [[Michael Sela]].<ref name=":1" /> Arnon joined the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] in 1960.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=האקדמיה הלאומית הישראלית למדעים The Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities  - Prof. Ruth Arnon |url=https://academy.ac.il/RichText/GeneralPage.aspx?nodeId=1439 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240423053306/https://academy.ac.il/RichText/GeneralPage.aspx?nodeId=1439 |archive-date=2024-04-23 |access-date=2026-09-24 |website=academy.ac.il |language=en|url-status=live}}</ref> She has focused most of her life on the field of immunology.<ref name=":2" /> While at Weizmann, Arnon served as the Head of the Department of Chemical Immunology (1975–1978), as the Dean of the Faculty of Biology (1985–1988), Director of the MacArthur Center for Parasitology (1984–1994), Vice President for International Scientific Relations (1995–1997), and as Vice President of the institute (1988–1992).<ref name=":2" /> In addition, Professor Arnon served as the Director of the institute's MacArthur Center for Molecular Biology of Tropical Diseases from 1985 to 1994.<ref name=":2" /> Much of Arnon's work has been in the development of vaccinations and cancer research.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Ruth Arnon Home Page |url=https://www.weizmann.ac.il/immunology/sci/ArnonPage.html |access-date=2026-09-27 |website=www.weizmann.ac.il}}</ref>  One of her largest contributions to science was working alongside Professor Michael Sela to develop a drug for multiple sclerosis called [[Copaxone]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=1997-05-01 |title=Cop 1 (Copaxone®): The Story of a Drug - Weizmann Wonder Wander - News, Features and Discoveries |url=https://wis-wander.weizmann.ac.il/life-sciences/cop-1-copaxone%C2%AE-story-drug |access-date=2026-09-27 |website=Weizmann Wonder Wander - News, Features and Discoveries from the Weizmann Institute of Science |language=en}}</ref> They, along with Devorah Tietelbaum who was at the time a doctoral student, discovered that a material synthetically produced in the lab could suppress a disease found in animals that is a model for multiple sclerosis. After thirty years of research Copaxone was approved for medical use.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ruth Arnon |url=https://jwa.org:443/encyclopedia/article/arnon-ruth |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=Jewish Women's Archive |language=en}}</ref>

Arnon served as the Chairperson of the Sciences division of the Israel Academy of Sciences from 1995 to 2001.<ref name=":2" /> She later was elected as President of the Israel Academy.<ref name=":2" /> She is also a member of the EMBO, the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]].<ref name=":2" />  Arnon served as Secretary-General of the International Union of Immunological Sciences, the President of the European Federation of Immunological Societies,<ref>{{Cite web |title=About |url=https://www.iis.org.il/about |access-date=2026-09-27 |website=welcome |language=en}}</ref> and is also a member of the European Union Research Advisory Board.<ref name=":2" />

Arnon has published more than four hundred articles in biochemistry and immunology.<ref name=":1" />

She was a visiting professor at the Rockefeller Institute (New York), University of Washington (Seattle), University of California (Los Angeles), Pasteur Institute (Paris), Walter and Elise Hall Institute (Melbourne), Imperial Cancer Research Fund (London), and the Curie Institute (Paris).<ref name=":1" />

===Copaxone===

Arnon and Sela developed a new drug application for the treatment of [[multiple sclerosis]] called Copolymer 1.  Its chemical name is glatiramer acetate.  It was submitted by the TEVA Pharmaceutical Company to the FDA for approval, under the name of [[Copaxone]], on June 14, 1995.<ref>{{Cite journal|pmid=8793553|year=1996|last1=Arnon|first1=R|title=The development of Cop 1 (Copaxone), an innovative drug for the treatment of multiple sclerosis: Personal reflections|journal=Immunology Letters|volume=50|issue=1–2|pages=1–15|doi=10.1016/0165-2478(96)02506-0}}</ref> Studies by Arnon et al. have shown an increase in [[myelination]] as a result of Cop 1.<ref>{{Cite journal|doi=10.1016/j.jneuroim.2014.08.573|title=Enhanced myelination in autoimmunity and in normal development induced by immunomodulatory treatment|journal=Journal of Neuroimmunology|volume=275|pages=213–214|year=2014|last1=Aharoni|first1=Rina|last2=Eilam|first2=Raya|last3=From|first3=Renana|last4=Bar Lev|first4=Dekel D.|last5=Sela|first5=Michael|last6=Arnon|first6=Ruth|issue=1–2|s2cid=53189444}}</ref>  In a 2004 article, Arnon and Aharoni state that glatiramer acetate is "highly effective in the suppression of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis in various species."<ref>{{cite journal | pmc=521994 | pmid=15371592 | doi=10.1073/pnas.0404887101 | volume=101 Suppl 2 | title=Mechanism of action of glatiramer acetate in multiple sclerosis and its potential for the development of new applications | year=2004 | journal= Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America| pages=14593–8 | last1 = Arnon | first1 = R | last2 = Aharoni | first2 = R| issue=Suppl 2 | bibcode=2004PNAS..10114593A | doi-access=free }}</ref>

===Current Research===
Arnon is researching a universal, recombinant influenza vaccination, as well as a cancer vaccine.  A 2009 paper discusses the use of [[virus-like particle]]s (VLP) to induce an immune response.<ref>={{Cite journal|pmid=19492960|year=2009|last1=Arnon|first1=R|title=Preclinical efficacy of a virus-like particle-based vaccine against avian influenza H5N1|journal=Future Microbiology|volume=4|issue=5|pages=503–5|last2=Ben-Yedidia|first2=T|doi=10.2217/fmb.09.33}}</ref> These particles cannot replicate, but possess the specific antigen-presenting proteins that immune cells use to identify viruses.  Therefore, a vaccine could introduce VLPs to an individual's immune system and bring about the production of memory cells.  Arnon and Ben-Yedidia hypothesize that these vaccines would be effective against [[H5N1]], a pandemic virus more commonly known as bird flu.  They have tested the various synthetic vaccinations on mice and observed a significant immune response.  In addition, they have put human lymphocytes in mice and also observed an immune response.<ref name=":4" /> Their research formed the basis of the company [[BiondVax]], who have taken the universal flu vaccine into human clinical trials.<ref name=":3" />

In 2017 Arnon was appointed co-chair of the UK-Israel Science Council, alongside [[Robert Winston|Prof. Lord Robert Winston]]. She has been a founding member of the council since 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.britishcouncil.org.il/en/Science-Council|title=UK-Israel Science Council {{!}} British Council|website=www.britishcouncil.org.il|language=en|access-date=2017-07-24}}</ref>

==Awards and recognition==
* 1979 – [[Robert Koch Prize]] in Medical Sciences, Germany<ref>[http://jwa.org/encyclopedia/article/arnon-ruth Ruth Arnon, Jewish Women's Archives]</ref>
* 1986 – Jimenez Diaz Award, Spain<ref name=":1" />
* 1990 – Elected Member of the [[Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=פרופ' רות ארנון |url=https://academy.ac.il/Index2/Entry.aspx?nodeId=752&entryId=18190 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260121164251/https://academy.ac.il/Index2/Entry.aspx?nodeId=752&entryId=18190 |archive-date=2026-01-21 |access-date=2026-09-28 |website=academy.ac.il |language=he}}</ref>
* 1994 – Chevalier de l'Ordre de la Légion d'Honneur, France<ref name=":1" />
* 1997 – Hadassah Women of Distinction Award<ref>{{Cite web |date=1997-01-28 |title='Women of Distinction' Award to Two Weizmann Institute Scientists - Weizmann Wonder Wander - News, Features and Discoveries |url=https://wis-wander.weizmann.ac.il/people/women-distinction-award-two-weizmann-institute-scientists |access-date=2026-09-28 |website=Weizmann Wonder Wander - News, Features and Discoveries from the Weizmann Institute of Science |language=en}}</ref>
* 1998 – [[Wolf Prize in Medicine]] for the development of Cop1, or [[Copaxone]]<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2018-12-10 |title=Ruth Arnon |url=https://wolffund.org.il/ruth-arnon/ |access-date=2026-09-28 |website=Wolf Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref>
* 1998 – Rothschild Prize in Life Sciences<ref>{{Cite web | title = Official site of the Rothschild Prize | url = http://www.yadhanadiv.org.il/node/608/view/recipients?field_rp_first_name_value=Ruth&field_rp_last_name_value=Arnon&date_filter%5Bvalue%5D%5Byear%5D=1998&date_filter%5Bvalue%5D%5Bmonth%5D=0&date_filter%5Bvalue%5D%5Bday%5D=0&date_filter%5Bvalue%5D%5Bhour%5D=0&date_filter%5Bvalue%5D%5Bminute%5D=0&date_filter%5Bvalue%5D%5Bsecond%5D=0&field_rp_category_value_many_to_one=life-sciences&field_rp_search_disciplines_value_many_to_one=All | access-date = 2013-10-17 | archive-date = 2016-03-13 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160313202437/http://www.yadhanadiv.org.il/node/608/view/recipients?date_filter&#91;value&#93;&#91;day&#93;=0&date_filter&#91;hour&#91;minute&#91;month&#91;second&#91;year&#93;=1998&field_rp_category_value_many_to_one=life-sciences&field_rp_first_name_value=ruth&field_rp_last_name_value=arnon&field_rp_search_disciplines_value_many_to_one=all | url-status = dead }}</ref>
* 2001 – [[Israel Prize]] in medicine<ref>The Gale Group. 2008. Professor Ruth Arnon. [Internet]. Weizmann Institute of Science, Department of Immunology; [cited 13 Apr 2015]</ref>
* 2009 – Elected member of the [[American Philosophical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://search.amphilsoc.org/memhist/search?creator=&title=&subject=2.+Biological+Sciences&subdiv=&mem=&year=&year-max=&dead=&keyword=&smode=advanced|title=APS Member History|website=search.amphilsoc.org|access-date=2019-04-07}}</ref>
* 2010 – First woman president of the [[Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-07-24 |title=Ruth Arnon {{!}} American Academy of Arts and Sciences |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/ruth-arnon |access-date=2026-09-28 |website=www.amacad.org |language=en}}</ref>
* 2020 – [[OurCrowd]] Maimonides Award for Lifetime Achievement in Science, Leadership and Menschlichkeit<ref>{{Cite web | title = 86-year-old Copaxone creator has no intention of slowing down | date=13 February 2020| url=https://www.jpost.com/HEALTH-SCIENCE/86-year-old-Copaxone-creator-has-no-intention-of-slowing-down-617544|access-date=2020-02-16}}</ref>
* 2021 – Honorary Officer of the [[Order of the British Empire]] (OBE)<ref>{{cite web |title=Honorary Awards to Foreign Nationals in 2021 |date=2021 |publisher=Gov.UK |url=https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/honorary-british-awards-to-foreign-nationals-2021/honorary-awards-to-foreign-nationals-in-2021}}</ref>
